When the bridge cannot do something, **adding a `[Tool]` method to a companion DLL is a
documented, supported path, not a hack** — it is where all 91 `jawa/` tools came from, and
59 of them were written in a single day.

⇒ **Use the `rimbridge-companion` skill.** It has the tool pattern, the
edit→build→deploy→test cycle (about **one minute** on a minimal mod list), the build
guards, and the traps that make a new tool silently absent.
`references/extending.md` keeps the lower-level assembly and csproj detail.
# Silent failures — engine calls that report success and change nothing

**This is the most expensive knowledge in the project.** Every entry was found by a tool
returning `success: true` while the game did not move, and every one is a call the RimWorld
API offers you with no warning. Measured live 2026-08-19 unless noted.

📁 **Which file am I in?** This one catalogues **ENGINE APIs** that mislead you.
`traps.md` catalogues **BRIDGE, CLIENT, BUILD and WORKFLOW** mistakes. If the thing that
lied to you was a RimWorld method, you are in the right place.

🔎 **This is a lookup, not a read.** `grep -i -n "<the method you called>" silent-failures.md`
— every entry names the call.

⚡ **The two that catch most people, before you go further:** nothing you write to a WORLD
is visible until `jawa/world_commit`, and nothing bulk-written to a MAP is consistent until
`jawa/map_commit`. If your write "did nothing", check that first.

🔑 **The pattern to internalise:** RimWorld's setters are frequently *advisory*. They write
a field and leave the consequences to a refresh you must know to call, or they refuse
conditions you must know to check. **Nothing throws.** So the discipline is always the
same — **write, then read back the RAW field, then look at the screen.**

---

## 1. Writes that need a refresh you must call yourself

| call | what silently doesn't happen | the fix |
|---|---|---|
| **anything touching a world tile** | nothing redraws. RimWorld has **no per-tile visual invalidation except pollution** | `jawa/world_commit` — a whole `WorldDrawLayer` mesh regeneration |
| **anything touching the map in bulk** | regions, rooms, path costs, reachability and power nets stay stale | `jawa/map_commit` |
| **`story.Childhood` / `Adulthood`** | disabled work types, skill disables, aptitudes and meditation focus all keep the OLD backstory. The setters only null a cache | **four** calls: `Notify_DisabledWorkTypesChanged`, `skills.Notify_SkillDisablesChanged`, `skills.DirtyAptitudes`, `MeditationFocusTypeAvailabilityCache.ClearFor` |
| **appearance fields** (head, body, hair, beard, colours) | the pawn keeps drawing its old face for the session | `pawn.Drawer.renderer.SetAllGraphicsDirty()` |
| **`WorldFeature.name` / `drawCenter` / `drawAngle`** | the OLD label text keeps drawing | `Find.WorldFeatures.textsCreated = false` |
| **substructure / foundation paint** | the overlay does not update | `Map.substructureGrid.MarkDirty()` |
| **bulk building spawn** | power nets stay unbuilt — the `Notify_*` calls only QUEUE delayed actions | `map.powerNetManager.UpdatePowerNetsAndConnections_First()` |

🔴 **The backstory one is the sharpest.** **RimWorld's own debug tool runs only the LAST of
those four calls.** Proven: doing all four moved a pawn's disabled-skill set from
`['Cooking']` to `['Social']`. Doing one leaves a pawn whose story says one thing and whose
work types say another.

---

## 2. Calls that refuse, quietly

| call | refuses when | symptom |
|---|---|---|
| **`equipment.AddEquipment`** | a Primary already exists | `Log.Error` and **nothing happens**. Call `MakeRoomFor(eq)` first |
| **`WorldGrid.OverlayRoad` / `OverlayRiver`** | the def is lower priority than what's there (`road.priority`, `river.degradeThreshold`) | the old def stays; no error |
| **`OverlayRoad(from,to,null)`** | always — removal is unsupported | `Log.ErrorOnce`. Removal means editing `potentialRoads`/`potentialRivers` on **both** endpoints |
| **`ageTracker.DebugSetAge`** | asked to go **backwards** — it walks birthdays forward only | 54 → 8 leaves the pawn at 54 **and reports success** |
| **`Zone.AddCell`** | impassable terrain, an existing zone, a blocking edifice | a short zone. Measured: a 6×6 stockpile took **11 of 36 cells** |
| **social `ThoughtDef` without an `otherPawn`** | always | the memory is dropped |
| **`TryAddOrTransfer`** | inventory full / unstorable | returns the **count moved** — it is an `int`, not a `bool` |

---

## 2b. 🔴 Tools that report a path, a name or a count they did not honour

Measured 2026-08-24, live, on the campaign world.

| call | what it reported | what actually happened |
|---|---|---|
| 🔴 **`rimworld/save_game` with `saveName`** | `success: true`, `path: …\Saves\ASHKARR_worldwork_2026_08_24.rws`, **`exists: true`**, `sizeBytes: 21258468` | **No such file was ever created.** The game wrote its CURRENT save slot — `WORLDMAP_V1_original.rws` — **overwriting it**. The `exists`/`sizeBytes` pair was stat'd against a file that is not the one named |
| **`jawa/world_tile_get`** | 200 rows for a 400-id request | **caps at 200 tiles per call.** It DOES set `truncated`, and that field is the only thing between you and a half-empty census |
| **`jawa/world_links_get`** | fewer edges than the world holds | **same 200-tile cap.** A 1,498-tile sweep in 200-chunks returned **915 road edges**; the same sweep in 100-chunks returned **1,224** — the true number. It reports `count` and `requested`, and they differ |

🔑 **The lesson is one line: an id-list tool answers about the ids it CHOSE, not the ids you
sent.** Compare `requested` against `count`, or diff the ids you asked for against the ids
you got back, on every bulk read. A census assembled from truncated chunks is not short by
an obvious amount — it is short by exactly the amount you will not notice.

⚠️ **And `save_game`'s entry contradicts a note in the `rimbridge` skill** that said
`saveName` "IS honoured — measured 2026-08-20". Both measurements are real; something
between them changed, or the 2026-08-20 test was run in a state where the current slot
happened to match. **Treat the written path as a claim and stat the Saves folder yourself.**

## 3. Getters that lie

| getter | lies because | read instead |
|---|---|---|
| **`SkillRecord.Level`** | **adds aptitudes**, so read-back ≠ what you wrote | `GetLevel(false)` |
| **`Tile.HillinessLabel`, `MinTemperature`, `MaxTemperature`, `Biomes`** | lazily cached with **no reset method anywhere in RimWorld** — stale for the session after any write | the raw fields: `hilliness`, `temperature`, `PrimaryBiome` |
| **`SurfaceTile.Roads` / `Rivers`** | biome-FILTERED views — `allowRoads ? potentialRoads : null`. A water biome **hides** links without deleting them | `potentialRoads` / `potentialRivers` to validate; the views only to answer "what does the player see" |
| **`RaidStrategyDef.Worker.CanUseWith`** | meaningless while `parms.faction` is **null** — every strategy reports unusable | resolve an attacker first |
| **`IncidentWorker.CanFireNow`** | carries storyteller **pacing** that `TryExecute` never consults | `false` does **not** block a raid. Just fire it | It also caches its result (and `CanFireNowSub`) per worker per game tick (`lastCheckCanRunTick`), forced calls included: a dry run re-asked in the same tick, e.g. after flipping a toggle on a paused game, replays the first answer. Step a tick (`S.run(5)`) between asks.

---

## 4. Constructors and factories that leave the object unusable

* 🔴 **`PrefabUtility.CreatePrefab` NEVER SETS `size`.** It comes back `(0,0)`, and `size`
  drives `GetRoot` and every bounds check — so `CanSpawnPrefab` refuses and `SpawnPrefab`
  cannot place. **A prefab captured with vanilla's own API is unusable until you set
  `size` yourself.**
* 🔴 **`ThingMaker.MakeThing` calls `PostMake`, which RANDOMISES HitPoints** from
  `def.startingHpRange`. Set HP **after** the spawn or it is silently overwritten.
* ⚠️ **`Frame.CompleteConstruction` and `Blueprint.TryReplaceWithSolidThing` hard-require a
  non-null worker `Pawn`** — NRE otherwise.

---

## 5. Rules that exist but are not enforced

* 🔴 **`GainTrait` checks NO conflicts, and `TraitSet` has NO trait cap.** Check
  `TraitDef.ConflictsWith` and `BackstoryDef.DisallowsTrait` yourself or a pawn ends up
  Kind *and* Psychopath.
* 🔴 **`WorldLandmarks.AddLandmark` never calls `LandmarkDef.IsValidTile`.** Measured on a
  settlement tile: verdict `False`, landmark added anyway. `IsValidTile` is the
  *generator's* rule, not a guard on the setter.
* 🔴 **A `Settlement` with a null faction is DESTROYED on load**, with only a warning.
* ⚠️ **Nothing validates appearance**: off-gender head types, gene-requiring heads and an
  adult body on a child all "work". Child body is forced only at load.
* ⚠️ **Non-player pawns ignore player forbid flags entirely** — `Thing.IsForbidden(faction)`
  returns false for any non-player faction. NPCs will eat the colony's meals.

---

## 6. Facts that cannot be checked offline

* 🔴 **`BiomeDef.allowRivers` / `allowRoads` are ABSENT from the def dump** — all 80 biomes
  report neither field — yet live they are `False` on `Ocean`, `IceSheet`, `GlacialPlain`.
* 🔴 **`WorldInfo.overallPopulation` and `landmarkDensity` are not scribed** — whatever you
  set, they revert on the next load.
* 📌 **`isThickRoof` lives under the `fields` sub-object** in the dump, not at top level.
  Easy to read as absent.
* 📌 **Never guess a defName.** 1,225 BackstoryDefs, 2,129 ThoughtDefs, 265 TraitDefs,
  336 TileMutatorDefs, 113 LandmarkDefs, 41 PawnRelationDefs. Four invented names failed
  in one session.
* 📌 **Only 9 of 41 `PawnRelationDef`s are storable.** `Sibling` and `Child` are **implied**
  — computed from the family graph, refused by `AddDirectRelation`.

---

## 7. Geometry that isn't what it looks like

* 🔴 **A contiguous tile-ID range is NOT a contiguous region on the globe.** Painting ids
  20000–23999 produced scattered rosettes; importing 0–21871 produced a hard diagonal seam.
  Use the neighbour graph, never id arithmetic.
* 🔴 **`SpawnPrefab` CENTRES on `pos`** — the min corner is `pos - ((size-1)/2)`.
* ⚠️ **Walls create no roof.** A room built from walls is open to the sky until roofed.

## 8. The house rule that falls out of all of this

> **Write → read back the RAW field → look at the screen.**
> Two instruments, always. `jawa/world_stats`' biome histogram and `jawa/pawn_get`'s
> `levelRaw` exist precisely so a write can be checked by something other than the writer.
> ⛔ **A tool returning `success: true` is not evidence.** It never was.

## `jawa/world_mutators_set` on any `GL_*` def — reports `added: 1`, changes nothing

Measured 2026-08-26 on six genuinely empty world tiles across six biome/hilliness
combinations. Every `GL_*` (Geological Landforms / Biome Transitions) write returned
`success: true, added: 1` and left the tile empty; a normal mutator landed on the same tile
in the same call. Nothing was logged, and no category conflict was possible.

⇒ **Not a bug.** Those defs are computed at display time and never enter
`Tile.mutatorsNullable`; the mod's `TileMutatorWorker_Landform` removes what `AddMutator`
appended. There is no way to author them and no reason to — landform assignment happens at
MAP generation from the tile's hilliness, topology and elevation.

🔑 The tell that they are live anyway: an in-game world-tile pane listing a feature that
`world_mutators_get` does not return for the same tile.

## `jawa/world_landmarks_set` — `isValidTile: false` on a landmark that was placed correctly

The validity array is evaluated AFTER the add, so it reports the landmark you just wrote.
`added >= 1` plus a read-back showing your def is the only trustworthy signal. Conversely a
landmark CAN be placed on a tile the engine considers invalid — the flag never blocks.

## `jawa/build_batch` — `placed` counts spawn attempts, not survivors

Measured 2026-08-26, full 582-mod list, one run of 8 calls / 81 ops.

```
reported: placed 4+1+1+3+3+1+3+65 = 81, failed: [] on every call
map held: 78
```

The three missing things were each **destroyed by a LATER op in the same run** whose multi-cell
footprint covered them — a `Table1x2c` (1×2) over a `DiningChair`, and a third `Shelf` over the
two before it. 🔴 **Both the destroying op and the destroyed op reported success.**

⇒ Diffing `placed` against `requested` — the obvious check, and the one a build-verification pass
will reach for — sees a perfect run.

✅ **FIXED and proven live 2026-08-29** (companion build 752662e511f4): the tool now returns
`survived` (counted after every op), `lostToLaterOps`, and `displaced[]` naming what each op
destroyed with `placedByThisBatch`; `refuseIfDisplaces: true` moves the offending op to
`failed[]` before it spawns. **Assert on `survived == requested`, never `placed`.** A cell-by-cell
read-back with `rimworld/get_cells_info` after `jawa/map_commit` remains the belt-and-braces
check when the batch matters.

⚠️ Also: `jawa/set_terrain_batch` and `jawa/set_roof_batch` take **`ops`** (`'<Def>:x,z,w,h'`
joined by `;`), NOT a `rect` parameter. Passing `rect` fails loudly — `success: false`,
*"ops is required"* — so this one is safe, but a compiler that emits `rect` loses every cell.

## `rimworld/get_cell_info` has no room object

It returns terrain, roof, fog, walkable, zone, areas, things and designations, and no room.
Read a room with `jawa/room_get` (Role, stats), a temperature with `jawa/cell_temperature` or
`jawa/thing_ambient_temp`, and a pawn's `StatDef` values with `jawa/pawn_stats` or `jawa/stat_explain`.
`jawa/pawn_get` returns no stats. `rimworld/select_pawn` is colonist-only and `Dialog_InfoCard` has
no parameterless constructor, so the UI route is shut.

## `jawa/fire_raid` — `resolved.faction` is the REQUEST, not what raided

Measured 2026-08-26, 582 mods.

```
{faction: "Jawa_FreeDroidEnclaves"}  -> resolved.faction "Jawa_FreeDroidEnclaves", success true
                                     -> 5 x Jawa_Blackstar_Grunt arrived, faction "Blackstar Company"
{faction: "Mechanoid"}               -> Totharth Mechhive arrived        (matches)
```

`IncidentWorker_RaidEnemy` refuses a faction that is not hostile to the player and picks its own —
correct engine behaviour. The Free Droid Enclaves are **Neutral** on this world
(`jawa/faction_relations_get`: 10 hostile / 14 neutral / 0 ally over 25 factions). 🔴 **The tool
echoes the request either way and never says it was overridden.**

⇒ **Census the ARRIVALS.** `jawa/list_pawns` before and after, diff the ids, group by `factionName`.
A raid test that reads `resolved` has not verified which faction raided.
- `jawa/fire_raid` (`JawaBenchEventTools.cs`) has no `JawaBenchAwareness.BridgeBegin` wrapper, unlike `fire_incident`/`raid_shape_fire`/`spawn_pawn`: a raid fired through it journals chain `incident:RaidEnemy` only and its pawns read `ourInvolvement` unknown. Use `jawa/fire_incident` when provenance matters, or wrap `fire_raid`.

## 🔴 `executed: true` with nothing spawned can be a MODAL DIALOG a mod pushed instead of the action

A bridge call reporting `executed: true` with no arrivals is not proof the incident engine
ran and chose zero — it can be a mod's own modal swallowing the call instead. Diff
`jawa/window_list_close` across the call before theorising about the engine
(`SIX_FACTIONS_NEVER_RAID_1`: cost days, and a per-world saved cooldown made the symptom
flip between sessions).

✅ **Fixed at the tool.** `jawa/fire_raid`, `jawa/fire_incident`, `jawa/storyteller_fire` and
`jawa/raid_shape_fire` now diff `Find.WindowStack` by `Window.ID` across the firing and
return `windowsOpened[]` + `blockedByDialog`; `success` is `executed && !blockedByDialog`.
**Read `blockedByDialog` before `executed`** (`FIRE_RAID_REPORTS_MODAL_1`).

## 🔴 `rimworld/set_time_speed` — reports the speed it set, and the game stays PAUSED

Measured 2026-08-26, quicktest map, no window forcing pause.

```
set_time_speed {speed: 3, ultraSpeedBoost: true}
  -> success true, timeSpeed "Superfast", ultraSpeedBoostAvailable true

get_cell_info -> state.paused TRUE, state.timeSpeed "Paused"
ticksGame over 6 real seconds: 5696 -> 5696          delta 0
after 5 further polls 20 s apart:  still 5696
```

`get_ui_state` showed `windowsForcePause: false`, `anyWindowAbsorbingAllInput: false`,
`programState: Playing`. Nothing was blocking it; the speed simply did not take.

⛔ **`rimworld/get_game_info` does not expose `paused` at all**, so the obvious check cannot see this.
🔑 **Read `rimworld/get_cell_info` → `state.paused` / `state.timeSpeed`**, and diff `ticksGame` across
a few real seconds. A speed that "was set" is not a game that is running.

✅ **`rimworld/step_game_ticks` works and is the reliable route.** Same session, immediately after:
`{ticks: 600}` → `status completed, completedTicks 600`, and `ticksGame` 5696 → **6296**. It is one
tick per Unity frame, so ~3 000 ticks is a few seconds of wall clock — budget for it, but it actually
advances the simulation. A test that needs time to pass should step rather than use the speed
control. Today, prefer `jawa/safe_advance` via `B.ticks(n)` (`validation_core._BridgeBase.ticks`),
which runs many ticks per frame. See `skills/live-debugging-proof-harness/references/lightspeed-authoring.md` §3.

✅ **`jawa/set_game_speed` actually moves time and is the other reliable route** — ticks +177
over 3 real seconds at Normal, 0 when Paused (2026-08-30, FOUNDRY). Prefer it over
`rimworld/set_time_speed` above; verify either one by tick DELTA across wall-clock, never the
return value.

## 🔴 `jawa/list_pawns` — `job` and `drafted` are ALWAYS null

Measured 2026-08-26, six player-faction pawns, same map, same second:

```
jawa/list_pawns      Lana job=None  Haplo job=None  Shouta job=None  ... every pawn, every row
rimworld/list_colonists   Lana job=LayDown   Haplo job=LayDown   Leblanc job=SocialRelax
```

The pawns were busy the whole time. The field exists on the row, reads `None`, and never populates —
`drafted` behaves the same way.

🔴 **This silently invalidates any behavioural test that watches what a pawn is DOING.** It cost a
full 7,200-tick sowing run here: both subjects read `job=None` across eight steps and the honest-
looking conclusion "neither pawn took a job" was an artefact of the field, not an observation. The
tell was reading a subject I did **not** create — the pre-existing quicktest colonists read `None`
too, which no theory about my spawns could explain.

✅ **Use `rimworld/list_colonists` for a pawn's current job** — colonists only, but it is populated.
`jawa/list_pawns` remains the right tool for the census it advertises (every pawn, all factions,
which `list_colonists` cannot do); just never for `job`.
**Classifying pawns from `list_pawns`.** A factionless wolf reads `hostile:false`; the colony Husky reads `isPlayer` true. A colonist is `isPlayer` AND `intelligence==Humanlike`; a predator is faction None + Animal + proximity. The rows carry no humanlike/drafted field (filter on `intelligence`, read job/drafted from `jawa/site_state`), and the `faction`/`factionName` key is OMITTED, not null, on an unowned pawn: test `row.get("faction") is None` (a filter requiring `"faction" in row`, or `faction=none`, counted 0 wildlife on a map holding 20) and cross-check against a `list_things` census. A vanilla flee and a mod's flee both answer `JobDefOf.Flee`, so attributing the job needs a setting-off arm.

## 🔴 A stale `Verse.FloatMenu` blocks every debug tool after it — and reports success

Measured 2026-08-27 over five runs of the same 772-wall job that painted 759, then
448, then 0, then 384, then 384. **The runs differed in nothing that mattered.** One
wall whose colour menu was left open absorbs input for every wall after it, and
`execute_debug_action` answers `success: true` the whole way down.

⛔ **`rimworld/get_context_menu_options` cannot see this window.** A `Verse.FloatMenu`
is not a "debug context menu" — the call answers *"No debug context menu is
available."* whether the menu is open or absent, so it reads as "the tool never
fired" in both cases. **Detect it through `rimworld/get_ui_layout` and look for a
surface of type `Verse.FloatMenu`.**

```python
def float_menu(rb):
    for s in rb.call("rimworld/get_ui_layout", {}).get("surfaces", []):
        if s.get("type") == "Verse.FloatMenu": return s
```

🔑 **Assert CLOSED before you open, not just open before you click.** A menu still
standing is the PREVIOUS target's, and clicking it applies the change to the wrong
thing while reporting success.

⇒ **Generalises to every UI-driven loop on this bridge.** When an automation that
worked starts missing partway through and never recovers, suspect a leftover modal
before you suspect the tool, the camera or the target.

## 🔴 A debug tool has a per-GAME-SESSION budget. ~380 for `T: Set Color`

Same session, same job, driven three ways: 250 + 134 + 0 across **three fresh
PROCESSES**. Reconnecting does not clear it; only the game does. After the budget the
menu never opens again and `active` still reads `true` on the node.

⇒ **Never plan a job of thousands of debug-tool invocations.** Find the non-debug
route first, and if there is none, budget the count and verify by looking.

## 🔴 `DebugToolsGeneral.SetColor` reads `UI.MouseCell()`, not a parameter

`Verse/DebugToolsGeneral.cs:549`. The x/z you pass `execute_debug_action` only places
the virtual mouse; the tool then colours **every Thing in that cell**, conduits
included. Two consequences: a cell must be reachable by the mouse, and you cannot
point this at a cell holding something you care about.

✅ **The way round paint entirely: colour with STUFF.** `GravshipHull` takes any
Metallic stuff and stuff carries colour — `MA_MegaBone` reads warm grey, `DinoChitin`
rich brown, `Bioferrite` dark plum, `KOTOR_AlloyBronzium` brass. One `jawa/build_batch`
per material, permanent, survives a reload, no dev tool. ⚠️ Rebuilding a cell WIPES
what shares it, so re-place the conduits from the layout afterwards.

## 🔴 A ZONE CANNOT CARRY TEXT — `createZone` ignores the label you give it

`jawa/map_zones {action:createZone, zone:"MY NOTE"}` returns `created: "Stockpile
zone 1"`. The label parameter is only read by `paintZone`/`deleteZone`, to FIND an
existing zone. So the "name a zone to write on the map" idea does not work.

✅ **What does carry readable text with a camera target is `jawa/send_letter`** —
`{label, text, x, z, letterDef}`. Click the letter and the camera jumps to what the
note is about. That is the only route to durable prose inside the game.
⚠️ It declares `x`/`z`, **not** `targetX`/`targetZ`.

## ⚠️ `jawa/list_things` truncates at `limit`, and the truncation reads as absence

Asked for a 4,034-cell rect with `limit: 1500` on a ship holding ~2,340 things, got
rows that did not include the decals I had just placed — and I concluded the placement
had silently failed. It had not; `get_cell_info` showed them. **Read `countMatched`,
never `len(things)`, and filter by `defName` when hunting for one kind.**

## 🔴 A mod's own spawn-grace guard silently no-ops `T: Destroy`

Alpha-team's Sandworm mod (`chezhou.creature.sandworm`, thing class
`SandWormLib.SandWormThing`) refuses a non-lethal destroy for a window right after
spawn: `execute_debug_action {"path":"Actions\\T: Destroy", thingId}` returned
`success: true` and `jawa/list_things` still matched it afterward — no error, no
`false`, nothing but `effects.logs` carrying `"[SandWorm] Ignored early non-lethal
vanish destroy during spawn grace period."`. **Read `effects.logs` on every
mutation, not just the top-level `success` field** — this is the same shape as
the envelope-vs-payload trap in §2 of the main skill, one layer further in. Fix:
wait (a few hundred ticks was enough here) and reissue the same Destroy call; it
worked cleanly once the grace period lapsed.

⚠️ **The same creature also self-relocates every tick the clock is stepped, even
while `paused: true`** — 600 explicitly-stepped ticks moved it ~60 tiles from its
spawn point toward the colony. `step_game_ticks` runs a Thing's normal AI/tick
logic regardless of whether the wall-clock speed reads Paused; "paused" describes
the UI speed control, not a freeze on everything with a `Tick()`. Spawn anything
with autonomous movement well clear of anything precious, and re-check its
position before assuming it is still where you left it.

## 🔴 `rimworld/step_game_ticks` silently truncates well below the ticks you asked for

Measured twice, two different numbers: **~2,800 ticks per ~10 s call** on one session
(2026-09-12) and **~600 ticks per call** on another (2026-09-21) — the cap is not a fixed
constant, it degrades with mod-list size and load. Either way the call returns
`success:false, status:"timedout"` **inside the payload** while the outer envelope still
reads `Status:2, Success:true`, and it reports `"Advanced N game tick(s)"` for whatever N
it actually managed — which reads exactly like success if you don't check `status`. A
prior session's "advanced 263,701 ticks, zero spawns" finding was almost certainly this
trap: the real engine clock never reached that count.

⇒ **Never issue one large tick-advance request.** Loop it, re-reading the real
`ticksGame` after every call until the target is reached — never trust your own running
counter, and never trust the reported N as proof that many ticks actually passed.

⚠️ **A long advance that does reach its target is itself the risk.** Owner, 2026-10-13:
*"warping ahead in time like that is an EXTREMELY risky proposition in the game. Almost
anything can happen."* Pass 7: 120k–280k ticks of real stepping on a 56 °C map starved all
six unfed colonists (Malnutrition), and the game ended with the run still stepping. Read
free colonists, their food need and the open letters **before and after** every advance.
Verdict rules for a run this disturbs: `skills/live-debugging-proof-harness/SKILL.md`.

## 🔴 `jawa/time_set_ticks` simulates nothing — yet every absolute-tick timer on the map sees the jump

It reassigns the clock: no needs, no incidents, no growth. But anything on the map dated by
an absolute tick ages by the whole jump at once. Pass 7 (2026-10-13): the Pyrelands site
builder jumped ~10 days to mid-summer noon on a generated map, so its loose ash and 6–9-day
filth had expired before the first sample and read as a mod FAIL
(`PYRE_SITE_CLOCK_REPAIR_ASH_EXPIRES_FIRST`). ⇒ **Set the clock BEFORE the map exists**
(the map is then born at that date), never on a populated or staged map whose time-dated
things are under test. `monitor_governor_build.md` gates it on a map with a free colonist.
- **A timer the FlowWorks sheet kernel counts in engine PULSES** (`RM_SheetMath Params.CropKillPulses`, the 1-week crop drowning) cannot be aged by a `jawa/time_set_ticks` jump, since a jump runs no pulse. Test it by compressing the delay (a setting) per debug_process 'compress first', never by jumping the clock.

## 🔴 The game-over letter cannot be dismissed through the bridge

`rimworld/dismiss_letter` refuses `GameEnded` ("Everyone is dead or gone", pass 7,
2026-10-13); **reloading the save cleared it.** Like any modal, it can leave later calls
reporting success while they act on nothing — after a colony loss, reload before the next row.

## 🔴 `jawa/spawn_batch` NREs on a pawn-race `ThingDef` — use `jawa/spawn_pawn` instead

`jawa/spawn_batch` throws an unhandled `NullReferenceException` (not a clean refusal)
when given a pawn-race `ThingDef` — it routes non-filth items through `GenSpawn`, which
cannot construct a `Pawn` from a bare `ThingDef` the way `ThingMaker.MakeThing` expects.
**`jawa/spawn_pawn`, addressed by `PawnKindDef`, is the correct tool for any
creature/pawn spawn** (2026-09-12).

## `jawa/list_things` — `faction`, not `factionName`

Reading the wrong key diagnosed a healthy player-owned ship as factionless for a full
hour (2026-09-09).

## `rimworld/click_cell` dispatches a real click but may select NOTHING

Selection can come back unchanged or stale. `rimworld/clear_selection` works reliably;
verify what actually got selected with `get_selection_semantics`, never with the gizmo
list alone (2026-09-09).

## A raw hediff-severity write via `jawa/pawn_health` never triggers vanilla's needs recompute

`remove` + `add` + set `Severity` directly does not fire `AddOrRemoveNeedsAsAppropriate()`
— that only runs once, from `HediffSet.AddDirect`, at whatever stage the hediff had when
first added. `HediffSet.DirtyCache` only refreshes the disabled-needs cache, not the
need-gating logic. A whole "need-gating FAILS" finding was this artefact, not a real
defect. **Test a stage-dependent mechanic via the real player path** (a bench recipe /
bill), not a raw severity poke (2026-09-09).

## `jawa/transporter_launch` — `dryRun` only guards ONE branch

`dryRun` short-circuits the "spawn a new pod" branch, but calling it with an existing
`transporterId` and `dryRun=true` falls through to a real `TryLaunch` — a documented
dry-run request can trigger a genuine launch. Standing check for any NEW bridge tool
with a dryRun/preview/simulate parameter: **the flag must be checked on EVERY mutating
branch**, not just the first one written (2026-09-13).

## 🔴 NO `jawa/*` tool can force a `DoBill` job — there is no bridge route to a recipe

`jawa/ordered_job` and `jawa/prioritized_work` both CONSTRUCT the Job from `jobDef` +
targets (their own doc-comments say so) and never call `WorkGiver_DoBill.JobOnThing`, so
`Job.bill` is null and `JobDriver_DoBill` reverts to Wait. There is no vanilla escape
hatch either — zero `[DebugAction]` in 1.6 source mentions bill/surgery/recipe, and
`jawa/debug_actions` states it EXECUTES NOTHING. This cost three live passes before
anyone read the tool source. **Read the bridge tool's source before briefing a session
to "force it via the bridge"** (2026-09-19, `BRIDGE_DOBILL_FORCE_TOOL_1`).

## 🔴 `jawa/map_drop` CRASHES the whole game — and any reply field that carries a `PlanetTile` does too

`jawa/map_drop` on a 622-mod game ended in a Mono stacktrace inside
`JsonConvert.SerializeObject` in `TcpConnection.SendMessageAsync` — the bridge died
serialising the RESPONSE after the Map was already destroyed, taking the process with
it. The drop itself may have succeeded; nothing survived to say so. **Treat `map_drop`
as a one-way call that ends the session**, never as mid-wave cleanup. It also declares
`mapIndex`, not `mapId`, while the neighbouring `jawa/set_current_map` declares `mapId`
not `mapIndex` — the two disagree and only the client's param guard catches it.

The root cause generalises: `Map.Tile` is a `PlanetTile` struct in 1.6, and
`PlanetTile.Tile` returns a `Tile` that points back at it, so putting one in a bridge
reply throws `Self referencing loop detected … Path result.X.tile.Tile` — **after** the
action already succeeded. **Every reply field must be a primitive**: `map.Tile.tileId`,
never `map.Tile` (2026-09-19/21).

## `rimworld/get_mod_settings` — `topLevelSettingCount: 0` for a settings class with STATIC fields

It reflects INSTANCE fields only. A `ModSettings` class whose fields are `static` reads
as empty even while `hasSettingsWindow: true` — "the settings screen exists" and "I
exercised the toggle" are different claims and only the first is measurable this way
(2026-09-19).

## `rimworld/select_pawn` refuses colony ANIMALS — `rimworld/click_cell` does not

`Pawn_AbilityTracker.GetGizmos()` gates on `IsColonyAnimal`, not
`IsColonistPlayerControlled`, so a tamed animal's ability gizmo is reachable via
`click_cell` → `selectionAfter.selectedObjects` → `list_selected_gizmos`/`execute_gizmo`,
even though `select_pawn` itself refuses the same animal outright. A whole item was once
blocked on the wrong door (2026-09-20).

## Hostile pawns standing on a map have no duty and will not attack

A spawned hostile does nothing until it is given a real `LordJob` — `jawa/lord_assault_spawn`
gives it `LordJob_AssaultColony`, and only then does the AI use its abilities, within
~1000 ticks. "They never engaged over 1260 ticks" was a missing Lord, not a broken
mechanic (2026-09-20).

## `jawa/grant_ability`'s `alreadyHad` field is a READ, not a boolean flag

It reads `Pawn_AbilityTracker` to probe whether a grant-on-tick comp fired. When the
comp is switched off it answers `"has no Pawn_AbilityTracker"` — a stronger negative than
`alreadyHad:false`, and worth distinguishing before concluding the grant failed
(2026-09-20).

## `jawa/list_pawns` nests health under `health.hediffs`, never a top-level `hediffs`

`row['hediffs']` returns `[]` for every pawn and reads as a working mechanism being
inert. Read `row['health']['hediffs']` (2026-09-21); it is present only when the call passes `includeHealth=True`, otherwise there are no hediffs in the row at all. Read the reply shape in `JawaBenchTerrainTools.cs` `ListPawns` before keying into any bridge reply.

## 🔴 `jawa/pawn_health` adding `WoundInfection` at severity 1.0 is IMMEDIATELY LETHAL — `success:true`, no warning, no corpse in the obvious place

Measured 2026-09-24, four separate pawns, four separate death letters, same exact
tick as the add. `{"pawn": p, "action":"add", "hediff":"WoundInfection", "severity": 1}`
returns `success:true, didWhat:"added WoundInfection to ..."` — and the pawn is
simply gone from every subsequent `jawa/list_pawns` census, `rimworld/list_colonists`,
and `jawa/pawn_get`, with **zero ticks elapsed** (`ticksGame` identical before and
after). No `dead:true` is ever observed on the subject because it never comes back
in a query at all. The tell is `jawa/letter_list`: each loss is preceded by a
`"Disease: Infection"` letter at the identical `arrivalTick` as the add, followed by
a `"Death: <name>"` letter — the kill happens **synchronously inside `AddHediff`**,
before any tick-based disease progression is even possible. Reproduced 4/4 across a
freshly-spawned `Colonist`-kind pawn, a freshly-spawned `RSW_Jawa`-kind pawn, an
existing non-drafted colonist, and an existing player-faction animal — not
race/kind-specific. Isolated by adding one hediff at a time: `Cut`,
`MissingBodyPart`, and `Bruise` on Brain are all safe; only `WoundInfection` kills.

⇒ **`WoundInfection`'s severity scale is evidently already at or past its own
lethal threshold at 1.0** — it is not a "gentle infection that develops over days"
when added this way; treat any `WoundInfection` add as pawn-destroying until a
lower severity is proven safe (untested — 1.0 was the first value tried and it was
already fatal every time). **Never add `WoundInfection` to a pawn you want to keep**
without testing a much lower severity on a disposable subject first, and never add
it as part of a batch of hediffs meant to exercise several guards at once — the
pawn is gone before the later calls in the batch even run, so a whole batch can
silently test nothing. Costly discovery: 4 pawns died finding this (`BACTA_TANK_CORE_1`,
2026-09-24) — none were saved, so the loss was recoverable by not saving, but the
next session may not be so lucky.

Covers src/RimMandrake/Utils/deploy_custom_mods.py plan-first then --apply, reading the plan and refusing another seat's files, what a `-` line means and rescuing a hand-edited game copy with --pull, validating with validate_patch.py using BOTH --live and --defs, DEPLOY_HOLD.txt for files undeployed on purpose, why a mod with no About.xml or packageId is not deployable, why a companion DLL cannot be written while the game runs, and how to tell whether a derived artifact is still CURRENT — fingerprint over timestamp, the folder-mtime and capturedUtc traps, the ModsConfig knownExpansions overcount, and empty def-type files that make a --defs check UNMEASURED rather than passed. "Written" and "the game can see it" are two claims ``` /custom_patches// ← source of truth, committed ↓ deploy_custom_mods.py C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\RimWorld\Mods\ ← what loads ``` The game names its own copy on every launch: `Adding mandrake.jawa.patches(C:\...\RimWorld\Mods\Jawa_Patches)`. **Nothing syncs them.** Editing only the repo means the change silently never reaches the game — no error, no red text, the def simply is not there. C# mods are built with `python3 src/RimMandrake/Utils/winbuild.py ` (stages on `D:\ClaudeWork\rimmandrake\build`, Windows dotnet, DLL and `.srchash` copied back as a pair). `D:\Luke\dev\RimMandrake` is a read-only mirror of origin/main: Windows tools read it, nothing writes it. 🔴 **A subagent's clean `dotnet build`/`validate_patch.py` pass, plus a real commit+push, is NOT proof the fix was deployed.** Twice in one wave a genuinely-fixed patch/DLL sat undeployed in the repo while a live re-test still showed the old failure. A mod can be deployed and inert (present on disk, absent from `ModsConfig.xml`, so it silently never spawns anything) for a long time before anyone notices; check both states independently, never infer one from the other. ## 2. Plan first. Always read the plan. ```bash python src/RimMandrake/Utils/deploy_custom_mods.py # plan only -- changes nothing python src/RimMandrake/Utils/deploy_custom_mods.py --apply # repo -> game, then self-verifies python src/RimMandrake/Utils/deploy_custom_mods.py --mod Jawa_Patches python src/RimMandrake/Utils/deploy_custom_mods.py --apply --prune # also delete deployed files gone from the repo ``` Safe by default, skips authoring-side files (`Source/`, `*.py`, `README.md`), warns when a mod is not enabled in `ModsConfig.xml`, verifies every copy, and exits non-zero while drift remains — so the plan doubles as a pre-flight check. 🔴 **`--apply` overwrites the game copy with whatever is in the repo *right now*, including another seat's half-finished work.** Five seats share this tree. > **Read the plan. `--apply` only if every listed file is yours.** A file you do not > recognise is a live hazard, not a todo — tell the owner before you write. ⚠️ **With no `--mod`, the walk is alphabetical and a 120s tool-call timeout can TRUNCATE it mid-list.** A run that stopped at "Cuisine" would have been read as "only Armoury drifts"; the real answer that day was 5 mods including one the caller owned. Redirect the run to a file and confirm it printed its final `Drift found` / `Everything in sync` line before believing any drift list. More traps for this section: [references/traps.md](references/traps.md) § 2. Plan first. Always read the plan.. ## 3. After deploying - **Restart RimWorld.** Defs are parsed once at startup; reloading a save does not pick up new XML. Adding brand-new defs is safe for an existing save; changing or removing a def a save already references is not. - **Enable compatibility-patch mods LAST in load order.** Patches apply in load order, so a fix-up mod loading before the mod it fixes patches a def that has not been redefined yet, and the redefine wins. Validation plan — what you owe whoever holds the game **A deploy ends with a validation plan, not with `--apply`.** You are almost never the seat that will see it work: a game load costs **23–30 minutes** and one game is shared by five seats, so whoever holds it needs your prediction, not a nudge to "have a look at the Jawa stuff". ### The six fields **1. The observable** — what a player SEES when it works. 🔴 A positive observation, never "no error"; absences are the cheapest thing in the world to produce by accident. **2. The route** — the exact call, defName or click path that produces it. **3. The prediction** — a number or specific string, written BEFORE the look. **4. The threshold** — what CLOSES it, and the minutia explicitly out of scope. An item with no threshold is inspected forever; one observation, not a battery. **5. Batch or solo** — most checks ride together; **a new assembly goes solo**, because if the load comes up wrong nobody can tell whether it was the DLL or the three def changes beside it. **6. What a FALSE PASS looks like** — the way this particular check lies. ``` PROVE EXPECT LIES ``` Three lines: the call, the expected reading, and how a pass could be false. 🔴 And first ask whether it needs the game at all — the default is source. Rule and false-pass catalogue: `skills/rimworld-modding/references/validation-plan.md`. ### The four ways a DEPLOY produces a false pass 1. **A successful write says nothing about the running game.** RimWorld parses defs and loads assemblies **once, at startup**. `--apply` reporting every file copied and verified is a statement about the filesystem; the process that matters read its copy minutes or hours ago. ⇒ **LIES** must name what the game last loaded and when, not what the plan printed. 2. **An assembly the game holds cannot be overwritten — and the failure is easy to file and forget.** Windows refuses with `WinError 1224` (§7), so the copy does not silently succeed; but the game folder is now carrying a **different build** from the repo, and nothing in the plan output distinguishes "same DLL" from "yesterday's DLL". **md5 both copies — it is the only way to know:** ```bash md5sum src//Assemblies/.dll "/mnt/c/Program Files (x86)/Steam/steamapps/common/RimWorld/Mods//Assemblies/.dll" ``` 3. **An unscoped `--apply` deployed more than you think.** Five seats share one working tree, so a bare `--apply` sweeps up whatever else is dirty — including another seat's half-finished work — and any breakage in that load gets attributed to your change. ⇒ **Scope every deploy: `--mod `**, and say in the plan which mods moved. 4. **"Deployed" and "live" are different words.** A folder under `Mods/` changes nothing until it is **enabled in the load order** (and, for a compatibility patch, enabled LAST — §8). The plan warns when a mod is absent from `ModsConfig.xml`; a plan that was not read is a mod that is on disk and inert. ### Worked example A Harmony patch shipped as a new DLL for `Jawa_Patches`, deployed in the shutdown window: ``` PROVE Spawn Jawa + MeleeWeapon_Vibroblade, spawn a muffalo, draft and attack; watch the combat log EXPECT A Jawa with a vibroblade attacks twice in the time a vanilla knife pawn attacks once · Cooldown 1.4s (was 2.6s); Player.log prints "[Jawa_Patches] 3 patches applied" LIES Game copy may be the PREVIOUS build if RimWorld was running at deploy (WinError 1224); md5 both DLLs before the load. Absent Harmony line = patch never applied, not "nothing to report". ``` ⚠️ **Write it in the same commit as the deploy.** The alternative is that whoever holds the game invents a check, and theirs will not carry your prediction — which is the field that turns a look into evidence. ## The deployed companion DLL runs behind source, and a missing tool is ambiguous A companion assembly deploys only in a game-down window, so the game copy drifts behind the repo for as long as the game stays up. Measured once at **166 tool names deployed against 238 built** — 670 KB of IL, everything written that day. ⇒ **A tool missing from `--list-tools` proves nothing on its own:** undeployed, gated out of the build, or genuinely absent all read identically. Disambiguate with `build.py`'s own `tool_surface()` over both DLLs. ⚠️ **That is a BYTE SCAN.** Its "added" list is untrustworthy — encoding differences make tools that shipped weeks ago look new. Trust it for `LOST` being empty and for a name being PRESENT; corroborate a gap with file size and the build commit stamped in the assembly. ⛔ **A `jawa/` literal written in PROSE inside a tool description becomes a phantom tool name**, which makes `build.py`'s "THIS DEPLOY WOULD REMOVE TOOLS" guard lie in both directions. This skill is how to build one that cannot lie to you, and how to spend a run so it finds **mod bugs**. **The problem this skill exists to fix.** The 2026-10-11 overnight validation of GimmeSomeSlack and FlowWorks produced 12 distinct live findings. **One** was a mod bug (the hose perf defect, fixed, 6x faster). The other eleven were harness, site or instrument faults. The owner called that validation "mostly ceremony". Two of those faults were worse than wasted time: the Verse.Log cap and the 1,000-entry journal ring meant **every earlier full-list log-budget PASS had been partly blind**. A harness that reads PASS when it could not see is worse than no harness. So the job has two halves, and you owe both: 1. **Make the instrument honest.** It reports UNMEASURED whenever it could not ask. 2. **Point it at the mod.** Spend the run on the places where the mod can actually be wrong, and write down what each run taught you in the mod's functional script. ## When this skill, when another | you are… | use | |---|---| | writing, running or reading a proof / validation script, or classifying its rows | **this skill** | | needing *a* map, a quicktest, or deciding bridge vs quicktest vs cold load | `rimworld-debug-testing` | | staging a scene for a human to LOOK at, or taking review screenshots | `rimworld-live-review` | | calling a bridge tool and it did nothing, or you need its exact params | `rimbridge` and `skills/rimbridge/references/traps.md` | | adding a new `[Tool]` to JawaBench | `rimbridge-companion` | | launching, swapping mod lists, reading the first exception at load | `rimworld-load-round`, `rimworld-start-prep` | | the debugging *process* itself: the first-script contract, the ladder, GPT consults | `design/RimMandrake/debug_process.md` (binding; this skill is its live-run half) | | deciding whether a live proof is the right test at all, or how much to run | `design/RimMandrake/testing_policy_2026-10-28.md` §2.8 (live proofs: helps, hurts, when it was a mistake) and §4 (maturity × risk table); tunables in `src/RimMandrake/rimflow/testing_policy.json` | ## The anatomy of a proof The worked examples are `src/RimMandrake/GimmeSomeSlack/northstar/proof_all.py` (105 rows) and `src/RimMandrake/FlowWorks/northstar/proof_hose.py` (66 rows). Their shared harness is `src/RimMandrake/Utils/validation_core.py`. More traps for this section: [references/traps.md](references/traps.md) § The anatomy of a proof. ## Row semantics: PASS, FAIL, UNMEASURED Every row has a **status** and a **class**. 🔴 **`modcheck record` knows six statuses:** PASS, SKIP, UNCOVERED and UNBUILT are OK; FAIL and UNMEASURED are not. Any other word (`RECORD`, `INFO`, `MEASURED`) reads RED; `record` now prints it by word and row id (`record.KNOWN_ROWS`). | status | means | never means | |---|---|---| | **PASS** | the check asked the game, got an answer, and the answer met the bar | "nothing went wrong" | | **FAIL** | it asked, got an answer, and the answer missed the bar | "the call errored" | | **UNMEASURED** | it **could not ask**: the site never got clear, the precondition never held, the journal lost entries, the sentinel died, a tool refused | a soft pass | 🔴 **"Could not ask" is UNMEASURED, never PASS.** This covers a failed bridge call, a `success: false`, a tool that is missing, a site that read back blocked, a dead log, a `lost > 0` tap, and fewer than the free colonists the block needs. Read the tool's own `success` / `foundCount` / `notFound` fields. Never substring a payload. An UNMEASURED row is not green. `debug_process.md` §6a: "UNMEASURED is not green". | class | the defect is in… | what fixes it | |---|---|---| | **MOD** | the mod's code, defs or settings | the mod | | **SITE** | the staged scene (terrain, giants, fog, pawns, geometry the mod rightly refuses) | the staging | | **HARNESS** | the script, the bridge, the instrument, the window it waits | the script | 🔴 **A row that ran after the colony died or the game dropped to the main menu is HARNESS/SITE and not counted**, whatever it reads; a map with no free colonist voids every row that waits on a job. Pass 7 (2026-10-13): 17 "FAIL"s after a menu drop and every row after a starvation were re-run, not scored. A harness or site row in a shared session is written **only when it is not PASS**. A green one becomes a site note (`validation_core.SHARED`). ⛔ **Never hand-edit a result JSON** to flip a row, not even to test how modcheck reads a status. Fix the harness so it emits the right status and rerun. A result that has been edited is deleted and rerun before anything is recorded. More traps for this section: [references/traps.md](references/traps.md) § Row semantics: PASS, FAIL, UNMEASURED. ## Sites, clearing, calm The owner's full list will not leave a map alone. Each block starts by making its site independent of the map, then **reads it back**: - **Re-calm before every block**, not once per run: wild animals respawn after a one-off non-colonist sweep (a predator downed two colonists mid-run), and map-gen insect hives throw their own NREs. Draft every colonist the block is not using, because idle colonists wander into sites fast. - **`clear_huge_plants` before every block** on an `RM_TheRot` map. Huge Things re-plans a giant's trunk blockers whenever they vanish while the plant stands, so a giant *outside* the rect re-blocks a site you just cleared. This happened on 2026-10-11: a map with 5,000+ blocker cells, and style_hose R1–R6 FAILed with "Space already occupied". - **`prepare_site` reads back.** A roof, rock, plant or ruin left in the rect is `UNMEASURED/SITE`, never a mod FAIL. Fog is cleared by a colonist's sight (`reveal`), not by `set_fog` alone. - **Sites must be disjoint**, with margin for the mod's real geometry. For a hose this is the ~4.4-cell straight lead-out. Aim at the target's real footprint cell. - **Water and sources: footprint plus 2 cells.** Check `jawa/flowworks_excavation_rect` (`includeTerrain`) for `isSource` / water first. A pit beside river sources filled by gravity and spoiled its row. A failed check exits UNMEASURED with a named reason. Detail, map culling and the fixture recipes: `references/sites-and-timing.md`. ## Timing windows: wait on the precondition, then start the clock A flat tick window measures whatever happened to be slowest, and that is usually not your mechanism. - **Read the window from the design's own contract**, half by half. For example: discovery ≤ 60 ticks, then transfer within one 250-tick pump cycle *after discovery*. A flat 260 ticks from the lay was shorter than the contract itself. Each half was stricter than the old window, not looser. - **Wait for the precondition, record how long it took, then start the clock.** On the full list a freshly built powered consumer reads `PowerOn=false` for ~100–170 ticks. Vanilla's power net switches it on later, not at spawn. A cycle timed from the build measures that gap, so the row records `pumpPoweredAfterTicks`. - **Bridge time is ticks, and a step is not the step you asked for.** See `skills/rimbridge/references/traps/lifecycle.md` for tick-keyed caches, overshoot and load races. - **Advance with `B.ticks(n)`, never with an advance-read-repeat loop.** `B.ticks` goes through `clockgate.advance_chunk` to `jawa/safe_advance`, which runs many ticks per frame. A raw `step_game_ticks` runs one tick per frame, and every poll round trip costs ~53 ms. Stop-on-condition (`B.until`) and sampling (`B.watch`) are PLANNED. Today's rule and the item ids are in `references/lightspeed-authoring.md` §3. ## Time advances and disturbances - **A long-duration property is compressed, or decomposed and INFERRED — never chased for hours** (owner, 2026-10-13). Shorten its timing constants to watch it in minutes, then restore and read back the shipped value; if that cannot reach it, verify the components and record the whole as INFERRED. *"we should not waste dozens of hours frantically testing for a single very-hard-to-demonstrate property of an otherwise checked out mod."* Full text: `design/RimMandrake/debug_process.md` § "Long-duration properties". - **Avoid long runs of game time.** Owner, 2026-10-13: *"long runs are possible but risky: they require more time, more monitoring, and fewer assumptions to succeed. Avoid them when possible unless it's a clear win for time efficiency compared to an alternative."* Pass 7's 120k–280k-tick waits starved the whole unfed colony. Never warp the clock on a populated map; set the season before mapgen. Mechanics: `skills/rimbridge/references/silent-failures.md`. - **Before and after every advance, read** free colonists alive and fed, and open letters (death, `GameEnded`). A dead colony ends the counted part of the run. - **Verdicts when something disturbs a row** are the owner's rules in `debug_process.md` § "Test disturbances": corrected anomaly with no damage may PASS; damage to the test → restart the row, never FAIL; **every** threat → logged plus a test-environment item; protected colonists only in rows labelled not about health/needs/damage/death. - **Watch the run, not just its result.** The owner expects a live pass to be monitored (e.g. a `Monitor` tailing `D:\ClaudeWork\rimmandrake\scratch\bridge_calls.jsonl` for `time_set_ticks`, `start_debug_game`, failures). What telemetry cannot see yet: `skills/telemetry/references/traps.md`. - **When the owner says something happened in the game, relay it to whoever drives the bridge at once, and name no cause until the log does.** Pass 7's deaths were first blamed on the clock jump; the death letters said Malnutrition. ## Log budgets: two ways to go blind, both reading as PASS 1. **Verse.Log stops ALL logging after 10,000 messages** (`StopLoggingAtMessageCount`; only `Log.Clear` resets it). A chatty mod reaches the cap within one session. Player.log and the bridge journal then both go silent while the game runs on. → `validation_core.log_revive(B)` at run start, and `log_alive(B)` (a sentinel warning read back) at the budget row. 2. **RimBridge's journal is a ring of the last 1,000 entries of every level.** An intimacy mod writes ~0.3 info lines/tick, so an end-of-run `list_logs` sees only the last ~3,400 ticks. → `validation_core.tap_start(B)`. The tap is polled after every tick step and load, and it counts the entries lost between polls. **A budget with `lost > 0` or a dead sentinel is UNMEASURED.** Charge an error to the mod only against a same-list control. Detail, the control-noise method and the known full-list noise: `references/log-budgets.md`. ## Perf readings: time the production function, live A perf selftest that times a **modelled** cost cannot see the real one. The hose port's offline perf row passed at 0.001 ms/tick while live it was 0.152 ms/tick, 3x the budget. A per-tick cache was being rebuilt once per laid reel, because each reel checked on its own staggered tick. Measure live with `jawa/map_comp_timing` on a map at least as big as the budget's scenario. Pair it with a work counter on the real inner call and with a can-fail. Detail: `references/perf.md`. ## Pre-port save fixtures When a port moves a class, job or def between mods, save the **old** build mid-job before the port deploys, and prove the new build loads it with the job still running. For example: `RM_PREPORT_HOSE_MIDCARRY_20261011.rws` and `…MIDRETRACT…` were loaded by `proof_hose.py --preport-save` and the job was still running 60 ticks after load. Back up the keepers first and stat-diff the Saves folder after: exactly the new files, 0 changed. Slow the carrier if the job would finish before your read. Use "presumed, unproven" when you did not trace it. Do not quietly fold an untraced row into the nearest proven one. 2. **Fix harness and site faults as a CLASS, not one at a time.** A full-list run surfaces 2–4 new harness assumptions per ~15-minute run. Before the second run, one fresh-context read-only audit of the whole fragility class found 8 at once. The class is camera, ticks, idle pawns, site margins, fog, save timing, log budget and tier. 3. **Then deliberately aim at the mod.** A green proof after harness fixes is not the end of the job. Ask where the mod could still be wrong that no row reads: - **leads**: for example, `Building_LiquidPump.TryDraw` loses the level if `TryAddLiquid` refuses, and nothing asserts it cannot happen; - **rows that have never been red**: a check never seen red proves nothing; - **conservation and accounting**: units in == units out; - **perf on the real hot path**; - **upgrade paths**: old saves, imported settings flags; - **the mod on the full list**: a mod that has only ever run on its 15-mod tier carries tier assumptions. Each answer becomes a row that **can go red**. 4. **Record what the run learned in the mod's functional script** (`debug_process.md` §0.4, §2.4). A check that goes red for the reported reason. A guard for each informative dead theory. `RULED OUT: — ` in the walk's `## anti-guessing notes`. Nothing that found a bug lives only in a Transient log. 5. **The commit names the class** (MOD / SITE / HARNESS) and the row id. A prior-pass-now-fail is a STOP: that regression is the finding, unless `git log --since=` on the subsystem's source shows a RULED behaviour change (liquid spill became `RM_Filth_WaterSpill`, so a row counting only `RM_Filth_LiquidSpill` failed). Search the map for every filth def the liquid can make before calling it lost. How to tell the classes apart, the 2026-10-11 tally and the modcheck/walk traps: `references/classifying-and-learning.md`. ## Before you trust any run - **Tier truth.** A proof labelled with a tier can run on a different list. On 2026-10-10 a "gimmesomeslack tier" run was really on 550 mods. Read `len(env.running)` and compare that number between runs, never the labels. - **Assembly identity.** Run from a clone or `git archive` export whose DLL is byte-identical to the deployed copy. A bench clone with an older DLL aborted v2 at L2. - **Staleness.** A recorded proof goes STALE when any mod-folder file changes, except `validation.py`, `human_review.py`, `northstar/` and whatever the mod lists in `.hashignore` (review tooling and art sources belong there). A loose `.py` in the mod root IS hashed. Finish every mod-folder edit before the run you will record. - **Owner rulings.** An owner ruling that *refuses* a behaviour invalidates every live site built before it. Re-check scene geometry against the ruling. The offline model stays green through that change, because it never modelled the refusal. #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Bounded P1 live proof on the all-DLC HugeThingsTestRaces + FlowWorks tier.

Uses an existing disposable calm save, a synthetic harness-only two-contact oak,
and grounded elephant test races. Never worldgen or flight. PROVE: distant pawn's
only corridor exit stays open; 100 sparse plants eventually realize their contacts
under the declared production scheduler cap; obstructed T3 conversion survives reload, retries
without wiping its obstruction, and cannot butcher around the site-only contract.
LIES: zero blockers / zero workload deferral, a pawn already trapped, a missing corpse,
a disabled site feature, accepted-but-not-executed orders, or absent controls cannot
pass. Restore the whole scene-begin save, verify its rectangle hash and all statics.
"""
import argparse
import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path
import re
import sys
import time

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = HERE.parents[3]
for p in (ROOT/'src/RimMandrake/Utils', ROOT/'src/RimMandrake/Utils/modcheck'):
    sys.path.insert(0, str(p))
import validation_core as V
import test_site_saves as T
import helpers as H
from game_paths import SAVES

MC = 'RimMandrake.HugeThings.MapComponent_HugeFootprints'
HOOKS = 'RimMandrake.TitanicCreatures.TitanValidationHooks'
SETTINGS = 'RimMandrake.HugeThings.RM_HugeThingsSettings'
PROOF = 'RimMandrake.FlowWorks.RM_PitPrisonProof'
RECT = '40,70,185,155'
BLOCKER = 'RM_HugeTrunkBlocker'
PLANT = 'RM_TestContactPlant'
SCHEDULER_SOURCE = (HERE.parent/'Source/MapComponent_HugeFootprints.cs').read_text(encoding='utf-8')
WORK_CAP = int(re.search(r'const int WorkUnitsPerTick = (\d+);', SCHEDULER_SOURCE)[1])
VISIT_CAP = int(re.search(r'const int RefreshesPerTick = (\d+);', SCHEDULER_SOURCE)[1])


def require(ok, why):
    if not ok:
        raise AssertionError(why)


def kv(txt):
    return dict(re.findall(r'(\w+)=([^\s|]+)', str(txt)))


class HarnessRefusal(RuntimeError):
    pass


class Run:
    def __init__(self, receipt):
        self.b = V.Bridge()
        self.rec = receipt
        self.prior = {}

    def call(self, tool, allow=False, **args):
        r = self.b.call(tool, **args)
        self.rec['calls'].append(dict(tool=tool, args=args, result=r))
        if not allow and r.get('success') is False:
            raise HarnessRefusal(f'{tool} refused: {r}')
        return r

    def sc(self, method, args='', typ=MC):
        r = self.call('jawa/static_call', type=typ, method=method, args=args)
        require('result' in r and not str(r['result']).startswith('FAIL'), str(r))
        return str(r['result'])

    def setting(self, field, value):
        if field not in self.prior:
            self.prior[field] = self.call('jawa/mod_settings_field', typeName=SETTINGS, field=field, action='get')['value']
        self.call('jawa/mod_settings_field', typeName=SETTINGS, field=field, action='set', value=str(value))
        got = self.call('jawa/mod_settings_field', typeName=SETTINGS, field=field, action='get')['value']
        require(str(got).lower() == str(value).lower(), f'{field} did not stick')

    def ticks(self, n):
        before = self.call('jawa/site_state')['ticksGame']
        self.b.ticks(n)
        after = self.call('jawa/site_state')['ticksGame']
        require(after-before == n, f'tick delta {after-before} != {n}')

    def things(self, defname, rect):
        r = self.call('jawa/list_things', defName=defname, rect=rect, limit=1000)
        require('things' in r and r.get('countMatched') == len(r['things']), f'incomplete census: {r}')
        return r['things']

    def stage(self, roots):
        r = self.call('jawa/artboard_stage', phase='subjects', pause=True, killHostiles=False,
                      ops='\n'.join(f'id=p{i}|kind=plant|x={x}|z={z}|def={PLANT}|growth=1' for i,(x,z) in enumerate(roots)))
        require(len(r.get('ops', [])) == len(roots) and all(x.get('ok') for x in r['ops']), f'plant staging: {r}')

    def reachable(self, pawn):
        # This tool issues an order even for waitTicks=0. Read CanReach as the answer,
        # stop immediately while paused, and require that no time or position changed.
        r = self.call('jawa/order_pawn', allow=True, pawnId=pawn, x=112, z=100,
                      pathEndMode='oncell', waitTicks=0, unpause=False, draft=True)
        self.call('jawa/stop_job', pawnId=pawn, mode='stopall')
        rows = r.get('pawns', [])
        require(len(rows)==1 and r.get('ticksElapsed')==0 and rows[0]['start']==rows[0]['end'], f'bad paused reach probe: {r}')
        return rows[0]['canReach'] is True

    def footprints(self):
        # Removing natural rock supports without its roof drops CollapsedRocks
        # during the closure clock, re-obstructing a successfully cleared site.
        self.call('jawa/set_roof_batch', ops='None:70,90,48,22;None:120,120,100,100')
        self.call('jawa/destroy_batch', categories='All', rects='70,90,48,22;120,120,100,100')
        self.call('jawa/set_terrain_batch', ops='Soil:70,90,48,22;Soil:120,120,100,100')
        walls = [(x,z) for x in range(75,101) for z in (99,101)] + [(75,100)]
        self.call('jawa/build_batch', ops=';'.join(f'Wall:{x},{z}' for x,z in walls), stuff='WoodLog', faction='player')
        p = self.call('jawa/spawn_pawn', kindDef='Colonist', x=77, z=100, faction='player', count=1, xenotype='Baseliner')['pawns']
        require(len(p)==1, str(p))
        pawn = p[0]['id']
        require(self.reachable(pawn), 'corridor pawn already trapped before plant')
        self.stage([(102,100)])
        self.ticks(120)
        probe = self.sc('DebugPlantState', 'current|102,100')
        self.rec['closure'] = dict(probe=probe, reachable=self.reachable(pawn), blockers=self.things(BLOCKER,'98,98,9,5'))
        f = kv(probe)
        require(f.get('claimed')=='2' and f.get('realized')=='1' and f.get('pending')=='1', f'closure has no positive realized/refused pair: {probe}')
        require(self.rec['closure']['reachable'] and len(self.things(BLOCKER,'100,100,1,1'))==0,
                'plant closed the distant pawn corridor')
        roots=[(130+8*x,130+8*z) for x in range(10) for z in range(10)]
        self.stage(roots)
        samples=[]
        for tick in range(1,241):
            self.ticks(1)
            txt=self.sc('DebugCounts','current')
            f=kv(txt)
            used, cap=map(int,f['work'].split('/'))
            require(cap==WORK_CAP and 0<=used<=cap and int(f['ownersVisited'])<=VISIT_CAP,
                    f'scheduler cap violated: {txt}')
            samples.append(dict(tick=tick, counts=txt))
            if int(f['realized'])>=201:
                break
        self.rec['budget_samples']=samples
        count=len(self.things(BLOCKER,'120,120,100,100'))
        require(int(kv(samples[0]['counts'])['realized'])<201, 'no deferred-work pressure on the first tick')
        self.rec['work_cap']=WORK_CAP
        self.rec['visit_cap']=VISIT_CAP
        self.rec['cap_exhaustion_observed']=any(int(kv(s['counts'])['budgetRefusals'])>0 for s in samples)
        # This live workload proves owner slicing and eventual realization. The
        # production-code offline harness separately forces exhaustion across maps;
        # a live counter that never hits its cap is not evidence of exhaustion.
        require(count==200, f'budget starvation: {count}/200 sparse contacts after {len(samples)} ticks')
        require(self.reachable(pawn), 'stress planting closed the corridor')
        self.rec['footprints']='PASS'

    def corpse(self, tx):
        self.setting('corpseSiteEnabled',True)
        self.setting('yieldCurveEnabled',False)
        gated=self.sc('ButcherYieldReport','RM_TestTitanT3Adult',HOOKS)
        require(kv(gated).get('meat')=='0' and kv(gated).get('leather')=='0', 'T3 bypass with curve off: '+gated)
        self.setting('corpseSiteEnabled',False)
        control=self.sc('ButcherYieldReport','RM_TestTitanT3Adult',HOOKS)
        require(int(kv(control)['meat'])>0, 'disabled-feature butcher control produced no meat')
        self.setting('corpseSiteEnabled',True)
        self.call('jawa/set_roof_batch', ops='None:46,166,9,9')
        self.call('jawa/destroy_batch', categories='All', rects='46,166,9,9')
        self.call('jawa/set_terrain_batch', ops='Soil:46,166,9,9')
        self.call('jawa/build_batch',ops='Wall:51,171',stuff='WoodLog',faction='player')
        wall=self.things('Wall','51,171,1,1')
        require(len(wall)==1, 'obstruction not built')
        before=int(kv(self.sc('SiteReport','',HOOKS))['sites'])
        killed=self.sc('KillTitanAt','RM_TestTitanT3Adult|50,170',HOOKS)
        corpse=kv(killed)['corpse']
        self.ticks(251)
        require(any(t['id']==corpse for t in self.things('Corpse_RM_TestTitanT3Adult','46,166,9,9')), 'blocked corpse disappeared')
        require(self.things('Wall','51,171,1,1')==wall, 'conversion wiped or damaged its obstruction')
        require(int(kv(self.sc('SiteReport','',HOOKS))['sites'])==before, 'blocked site converted')
        name='CODEX_HugeP1_Occupied_'+time.strftime('%Y%m%dT%H%M%S')
        self.rec['occupied_save']=T.save_site(self.call,name,SAVES)
        loaded=T.load_site(self.call,'calm',name=name,check=False,map_controls=('modal_broker',))
        self.rec['occupied_load']=loaded
        require(loaded['verified'],str(loaded))
        H.quiet_world(T.call_session(self.call),tx,wild_spawner=False,log_raids=False)
        require(any(t['id']==corpse for t in self.things('Corpse_RM_TestTitanT3Adult','46,166,9,9')), 'corpse lost on occupied reload')
        require(self.things('Wall','51,171,1,1')==wall, 'obstruction lost on reload')
        self.call('jawa/destroy_batch',categories='All',rects='51,171,1,1')
        self.ticks(251)
        after=self.sc('SiteReport','',HOOKS)
        require(not self.things('Corpse_RM_TestTitanT3Adult','46,166,9,9'), 'conversion never retried')
        require(int(kv(after)['sites'])==before+1 and int(kv(after)['meat'])>0, 'site lacks raw harvest pool: '+after)
        self.rec['corpse']=dict(status='PASS',butcher_gated=gated,butcher_control=control,killed=killed,site=after,obstruction=wall)


def main():
    ap=argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument('--out',required=True)
    a=ap.parse_args()
    rec=dict(script=__file__,calls=[],started=time.time(),scope='isolated 14-mod all-DLC synthetic-plant/grounded-elephant fixture')
    r=Run(rec)
    snap='CODEX_HugeP1_Begin_'+time.strftime('%Y%m%dT%H%M%S')
    saved=False
    baseline=None
    tx=None
    rec['artifact_sha256']=hashlib.sha256((HERE.parent/'Assemblies/RM_HugeThings.dll').read_bytes()).hexdigest()
    try:
        loaded=T.load_site(r.call,'calm')
        require(loaded['verified'],str(loaded))
        rec['snapshot']=T.save_site(r.call,snap,SAVES)
        saved=True
        require(T.load_site(r.call,'calm',name=snap,check=False)['verified'],'initial snapshot reload failed')
        baseline=r.sc('Rect',RECT,PROOF)
        rec['baseline']=baseline
        tx=H.SettingsTransaction(T.call_session(r.call))
        tx.__enter__()
        rec['quiet']=H.quiet_world(T.call_session(r.call),tx,wild_spawner=False,log_raids=False)
        for field,value in dict(giantPlantsEnabled=True,plantTrunkEnabled=True,plantTrunkScale=1,giantAnimalsEnabled=True).items():
            r.setting(field,value)
        r.footprints()
        r.corpse(tx)
        rec['status']='PASS'
    except Exception as ex:
        rec['status']='UNMEASURED' if isinstance(ex,HarnessRefusal) else 'FAIL'
        rec['failure_class']='HARNESS' if isinstance(ex,HarnessRefusal) else 'MOD_OR_SITE_ASSERTION'
        rec['error']=repr(ex)
    finally:
        errors=[]
        if saved:
            try:
                rec['restore_load']=T.load_site(r.call,'calm',name=snap,check=False)
                require(rec['restore_load']['verified'],'snapshot did not reload')
                rec['restore_hash']=r.sc('Rect',RECT,PROOF)
                require(baseline is not None and rec['restore_hash']==baseline,'snapshot rectangle hash differs')
            except Exception as ex: errors.append(repr(ex))
        rec['restore_settings']={}
        for field,value in r.prior.items():
            try:
                r.setting(field,value)
                rec['restore_settings'][field]=value
            except Exception as ex: errors.append(repr(ex))
        if tx:
            try: tx.__exit__(None,None,None)
            except Exception as ex: errors.append(repr(ex))
        rec['restore_errors']=errors
        if errors: rec['status']='FAIL'
        rec['finished']=time.time()
        Path(a.out).write_text(json.dumps(rec,indent=2,default=str),encoding='utf-8')
        print(rec['status'],rec.get('error',''),errors,flush=True)
    return 0 if rec['status']=='PASS' else 1


if __name__=='__main__':
    sys.exit(main())

    python.exe src/RimMandrake/Utils/modcheck/test_site_saves.py list
    python.exe src/RimMandrake/Utils/modcheck/test_site_saves.py build calm            # fresh quicktest -> clean -> save
    python.exe src/RimMandrake/Utils/modcheck/test_site_saves.py build river           # + river_site.py, home map dropped
    python.exe src/RimMandrake/Utils/modcheck/test_site_saves.py build pyrelands --fingerprint 417df172fdb5 --from-tag r6
    python.exe src/RimMandrake/Utils/modcheck/test_site_saves.py load calm             # load + read-back check
    python.exe src/RimMandrake/Utils/modcheck/test_site_saves.py check calm            # read-back on the current map
    python.exe src/RimMandrake/Utils/modcheck/test_site_saves.py prove river --build-if-missing  # A1 header [+ A2 load unless --no-load], exit 0/1

The suites call load_site() themselves by default (proof_all.py, validation_v2.py, extension_proof.py --site river);
each keeps a --fresh-map flag for the old path. Pyrelands keeps its own fixture loader (northstar_site.py
--reload-only --tag calm), which this module's `build pyrelands` feeds.

Two clean profiles:
  calm    every map-gen danger AND every unowned artificial building (ruins), for suites whose subject is not the
          map's own content (GSS, FlowWorks).
  danger  only the dangers (ancient-danger containers with their contents, triggers, hostiles, hives, explosives), for
          a biome suite whose subject IS the map (Pyrelands reads its ruins and its wildlife census).
Both: every fog/proximity trigger + signal action disarmed, the whole map unfogged with the re-sweep
(testenv_guards.clear_map_fog), the map-only quiet profile, Clear weather, no fire, queue cleared.
The ancient-danger CONTAINERS go by Vanish (Building_Casket.Destroy(Vanish) -> innerContainer.ClearAndDestroyContents:
the sleepers in a casket are destroyed with it, never dropped) BEFORE the unfog (owner 2026-10-15: "The pawns that emerge
from an ancient danger (hidden site on the map) may not be there before you open it, not sure.").

`call` is anything shaped call(tool, **params) -> dict (a bridge client's .call, rimdrive Session.call, a fake).
"""
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import sys
